name: SUM and REPLACE
description: Let D ( x ) be the number of positive divisors of a positive integer x . For example, D (2) = 2 ( 2 is divisible by 1 and 2 ), D (6) = 4 ( 6 is divisible by 1 , 2 , 3 and 6 ). You are given an array a of n integers. You have to process two types of queries: REPLACE l r — for every replace a i with D ( a i ) ; SUM l r — calculate . Print the answer for each SUM query.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and m ( 1 ≤ n , m ≤ 3·10 5 ) — the number of elements in the array and the number of queries to process, respectively. The second line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 6 ) — the elements of the array. Then m lines follow, each containing 3 integers t i , l i , r i denoting i -th query. If t i = 1 , then i -th query is REPLACE l i r i , otherwise it's SUM l i r i ( 1 ≤ t i ≤ 2 , 1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ n ). There is at least one SUM query.
output_specification: For each SUM query print the answer to it.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 920F — SUM and REPLACE [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
